messages:
Nina P.: Quick follow-up from today's infra section — thanks for the clarity. A few practical questions: 1) what's the plan for APAC node prewarming vs on-demand spin-up? 2) how will we prioritize customers for limited prewarm slots? 3) any ETA on the cost delta we should show in Console for routes using prewarm/spot?
Rory T.: Short answers: prewarm = keep minimal warm pool per-region for low-latency tiers. on-demand = spin-up with fast provision path. target for apac-sin prewarm pilot is mid-June.
Diego M.: On prioritization: we plan to tier customers by SLA + historical QPS. Tier A (SLA-backed) gets guaranteed prewarm capacity, Tier B can opt into best-effort prewarm, Tier C is on-demand only. still finalizing thresholds.
Elena V.: Can we add an opt-in flag so PMs/SEs can request prewarm for specific routes? Asking because some teams need consistent p95 latency.
Rory T.: yes — Console flag `prewarm: guaranteed|best-effort|off` will be in the next release. default is `off` for Hosted users.
Nina P.: How big is the warm pool per region? what's the unit (nodes, vGPUs)?
Diego M.: Pilot config will use node-counts mapped to route concurrency. e.g., 4 vGPUs for a small warm pool (supports ~200 concurrent low-latency sessions). we'll publish a sizing table.
Elena V.: About cost visibility: ProductOps, can we show an estimated monthly cost delta if a customer enables `prewarm: guaranteed`? even a rough number helps sales/SEs.
ProductOps: Agreed. we'll add an estimated cost line in route settings and an API field `estimated_prewarm_cost`. Need inputs from infra on per-node hourly rates.
Rory T.: For spot vs reserved fallback: priority order will be reserved -> dedicated reserved pool -> spot/ephemeral -> cross-region fallback. Spot is lowest preference due to preemption risk.
Nina P.: If a route falls back cross-region, do we auto-notify the customer or just surface a Console banner?
Diego M.: Both. Console banner + an optional webhook event `routing.fallback` customers can subscribe to. will include reason and latency delta.
Elena V.: Any mitigation for cache-warmth when traffic hops regions? cold KV caches were noisy last month.
Rory T.: We're shipping a cross-region prefix cache replication prototype (async). initial rollout to critical datasets only. reduces cache misses on failover.
Nina P.: Can someone paste the prewarm policy sample we'll ship so SEs can see what to tell customers?
Diego M.: Sample below:
```
prewarm_policy:
  route: realtime-chat
  mode: guaranteed
  nodes: 4
  min_uptime_minutes: 30
  cost_center: team-redwood
```
Elena V.: Nice. Any SLO changes? If prewarm guaranteed is used, latency SLO should be tighter.
Rory T.: We'll have two latency buckets: `primary` (prewarm/primary region) and `fallback` (cross-region or spot). primary p95 target 200ms, fallback p95 target 350ms. document in infra SLOs.
ProductOps: Action items from thread:
- Add Console cost estimate UI for prewarm (Owner: ProductOps, due: 2 weeks)
- Publish prewarm sizing table + sample policy (Owner: Diego M., due: 1 week)
- Implement `prewarm` route flag in Console + API (Owner: Elena V., ETA: next release)
- Hook up `routing.fallback` webhook + banner (Owner: Rory T., infra ticket INF-920)
- Cross-region prefix cache prototype rollout (Owner: Rory T., follow-up)
Nina P.: Please add SE playbook line: "when to recommend guaranteed prewarm vs best-effort".
ProductOps: Will do.
InfraBot: Ticket INF-920 created by Rory T. (prewarm-feature-and-fallback-webhook)
Diego M.: Also note procurement update: extra A100s delayed by 2 weeks. affects larger reserved pool growth but not pilot prewarm. procurement will send final ETA Friday.
Nina P.: Thanks all. I'll share this thread with the SE leads and schedule a short 30m run-through to align messaging.
Elena V.: :thumbsup:
